title: The Pile: An 800GB Dataset of Diverse Text for Language Modeling

content.text: Ideally we would train a GPT-3 model from scratch on the Pile and compare the difference in loss per dataset with that of the original GPT-3. Because of resource constraints, we instead use a GPT-2 model trained from scratch on the Pile

comments.html: GPT-3 è stato il primo modello di OpenAI a non essere stato rilasciato interamente.

content.text: Since GPT2-Pile was trained on both OWT2 and the dataset we are evaluating, we expect the second term in ∆set to reflect the difference in the intrinsic difficulty of the two datasets. Thus the total value of ∆set reflects how much harder the dataset we are evaluating was for GPT-3 than OWT2, minus the relative difficulty of the two tasks. As GPT-3 was trained on data very similar to OWT2, this gives us a proxy for how much better GPT-3 would do if it were trained on the Pile.

comments.html:
Perché utilizziamo il logaritmo?

Un Language Model non deve prevedere soltanto un token, ma un'intera sequenza e la probabilità dell'intera sequenza si calcola utilizzando la regola della catena:

\[ P_\theta(x_1,\ldots,x_T) = \prod_{t=1}^{T}P_\theta(x_t\mid x_{<t}) \]

Ma con migliaia di token il prodotto diventa estremamente piccolo, avvicinandosi rapidamente a zero.

Per questo utilizziamo il logaritmo naturale.
